Name: Matthew Manning
Question: What is your opinion on abortion?
Answer: I’m going to say something that nobody likes saying or hearing: The real reason the left wants abortion to be legal is because abortion absolves women from the primary consequence of sex: pregnancy. Forget the medically extreme cases here. Yes, a small percentage of abortions are done because the mother’s life is severely in danger. Yes, an even smaller percentage of abortions are done because the fetus is already dead. The vast majority of abortions are done out of what boils down to convenience. I’m 17. I’ve already experienced this attitude toward abortion multiple times from female friends who’ve had pregnancy scares. “If I’m pregnant, I’m getting an abortion.” They’ve said. With no hesitation. It was as casual for them as deciding to get their appendix out. Probably even more so. Don’t believe me? Take a look at this meme I found scrolling through Instagram the other day: Sure, call it anecdotal evidence. Even though the tweet has 15.4k likes, and the picture has 7,262 likes. And no, the person tweeting doesn’t run that meme account, so it’s unlikely those likes overlap. But it is anecdotal, and I can’t dispute that. Instead, I can show you the cold, hard, statistics: roughly 74% of abortions are done out of convenience to the mother. Sure, those statistics are from 2004. But the attitude toward abortions has only become more casual over the last 14 years. And those statistics are from self-reporting would-be mothers. I’d imagine women having abortions for convenience reasons are less eager to report that than those who aren’t. I want to clarify that I’m not dismissing the predicament these women are in by calling their decision to get an abortion “convenience based.” A lot of these reasons are financially or emotionally driven, and I do empathize with the women who are in these situations. Having a child will uproot your life in ways very few things can. But the fact that your life will be negatively impacted by your child does not give you the right to kill it. Not having sex before marriage originated for exactly this reason: to protect against the negative consequences of sex, primarily pregnancy. The left is in a position where they want to tell women that sex can be fun and consequence-free, when that simply has never been the reality. Legal abortion is a way to mediate the consequences and further “liberate” women. At this point, the problem isn’t just in banning or legalizing abortion. Completely depriving women of abortions at this point would only mean hundreds of thousands of more unwanted children born each year. The problem lies in the societal attitude toward abortion, and toward child-rearing and adopting responsibility in general. There would need to be a massive cultural shift in order to reduce the 600,000+ abortions that are currently being had every year. The vast majority of which are, again, being done for convenience sake. My opinion on abortion is that is it a symptom and enabler of a massively flawed societal viewpoint. A deep-rooted social attitude that has driven and continues to drive the destruction of the family unit. One that I’m not certain of how to solve. But what I am certain of is that the overwhelming majority of abortions are murder. And not murders of passion; murders driven simply by convenience. If that doesn’t send a bit of a chill down your spine, I don’t know what will.

Question: How real is the belief that many colleges are fiercely liberal and are extremely unwelcoming to conservative thought?
Answer: I’ve never been to college. But I did go to a private high school in the very liberal state of Massachusetts, with a lot of my teachers being former college professors. If the average college professor is anything like the teachers I had, I have no doubt that colleges are just as hostile to conservative thought as right-wing sources would have us believe. The day after Trump won the election, every single teacher I had threw out their entire curriculum for the day. They all encouraged us to have long discussions on our feelings about the president elect, and gave a large amount of sympathy to the people with the most dramatic sob stories. One kid in my English class voiced his support for Trump. A lot of the kids immediately started lambasting him as a racist and a sexist. My english teacher said nothing for several minutes. Eventually, the discussion got heated to a point where the teacher deemed it was unacceptable. Her reaction was to move on and give the floor to a different kid, without acknowledging the ad-hominem attacks on the Trump supporter. After class, she had the attacking students stay behind. She applauded them for their “courage” but suggested they be more polite in the future. That talk was apparently very stern, because it took less than 2 minutes. After that the kids walked out of her classroom and joined everyone else at lunch, where a lot of people praised them and continued to shit talk the Trump supporter. As the year went on, Trump jokes became a staple of nearly every teacher I had. It was impossible to go a week without hearing at least two teachers rant about their disapproval for him. The kids who joined in on these jokes and rants often became the favorites of those teachers, regardless of their grades or class participation. That one vocal pro-Trump kid could never get a teacher to like him, and they would even shit talk him to me and other kids privately. Students who wrote papers agreeing with their teachers, making comparisons between Trump and whatever villain/dictator we were reading about, were applauded. I don’t know if that was reflected in their grades, but it definitely made their teachers like them more. And let’s not be blind here; this isn’t necessarily an inherent trait of liberals and progressives. Some liberals are not hostile to those with different viewpoints. And some conservatives are. But people naturally gravitate toward those with similar opinions and world views. So when you’re in an environment where the overwhelming majority of both your teachers and classmates disagree with your views, and when you’re in a political climate as polarized as ours, you’re going to suffer. Partially due to outright hostility from your classmates (and some more extreme teachers), but more importantly because of favoritism that your views will disqualify you from the minute you vocalize them.

Question: What do you think is the worst fad of 2017 so far?
Answer: Hating Jake Paul Yeah, we get it. He's an asshole. He’s annoying. He’s seemingly unavoidable. But do you know what makes him unavoidable? People talking about how annoying he is. Jake is not some run-of-the-mill idiot. He's a troll. The stupid and cringey things he does are intended to cause controversy. He wants people to make reaction videos, he wants people to talk about how stupid he is, how he’s getting evicted, how he cheated on his girlfriend, etc etc. Why? Because that grows his audience. Let’s take a look at Jake’s YouTube stats since all of this controversy started (around June of this year): Look at how fast this kid has been growing. He was at 5 million subscribers in May, and now he's at 9.7 million just a few months later. Believe me when I tell you it's 100% intentional what he's doing. He even said in one of his vlogs that “when they hate, the bank account grows!” And he's right! Look at this picture (that I took just now) from his most popular (and most controversial) video: You might be thinking “wow, look at that like to dislike ratio! People hate this guy!” But what you should be looking at is the views. This video is monetized. The money Jake makes isn't based on how many likes or dislikes he has, or even how many subscribers he has; he makes money based on how many views he gets. In fact, are you curious as to just how much money Jake makes off of just this one channel? That's right folks. Anywhere between 1.4 and 22.2 million dollars a year. And considering the fact that he has a second channel, gets 20% of the profits from about half a dozen of his friend’s channels, sells merchandise, and up until recently got a nice monthly paycheck from Disney, Jake probably makes more money in a month than most people will see in their entire lives. So what should you do if you want Jake Paul to go away? Stop talking about him. He wants you to hate. He thrives on attention. He's like tinker bell, except instead of needing everyone to believe in him he needs everyone to talk about him. If you want the troll to die, stop feeding it. EDIT: Yes, I was aware before writing this answer I would be giving Jake Paul more exposure. I’m fairly ambivalent to Jake Paul; I don’t think he's a good person, but I don't care whether or not he grows. If people want to follow him that's none of my business. But seeing other answers about Jake Paul being the worst fad of 2017 was what prompted me to write this answer, as many people hate on him without realizing that grows his audience.
